topic: Shadow map light-space texel-grid snapping vs continuous unsnapped shadow swimming
topic_zh: 平行光阴影贴图纹素网格整数对齐与未对齐边缘蠕动闪烁（Shadow Swimming）对比
scope: Deterministic Light-Space Texel-Grid Snapping (quantizing orthographic shadow frustum center to integer multiples of Delta_texel = 2*R/N) versus continuous unsnapped frustum tracking across 17 sub-texel camera pan steps. No neural shadow synthesis execution.

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating Node CPU runs after warmup. O(1) reciprocal texel-size floor snapping versus 64-texel viewport lattice construction and linear scan.

protocol.function: C_snap = ⌊C_raw / Δ_texel + 0.5⌋ · Δ_texel → X_shadow(k) ≡ 1.0000m (0.0000m shadow edge crawl)

robustness.name: Sampled sub-texel camera pan steps pin the static world shadow boundary at 1.0000m

good_fit: Cascaded Shadow Maps (CSM) for directional sunlight in outdoor cities, terrains, and architectural walkthroughs
Explaining why sub-texel frustum translations make static shadow edges crawl by up to 1 full texel width
Locking orthographic cascade width to a rotation-invariant bounding sphere diameter 2*R before texel snapping
O(1) light-space translation snapping C_snap = floor(C_raw / Delta_texel + 0.5) * Delta_texel in the shadow matrix
not_for: Moving or rotating directional lights (e.g., fast time-of-day sun lapse) where shadows physically move across the ground
Local point/spot lights with fixed world-space frustums that do not translate with the viewer camera
Ray-traced hard/soft shadows (DXR / Vulkan Ray Query) that do not rasterize a discrete light-space depth grid
